learningJourney.title: What is a Rolling Deployment
learningJourney.explanation:
A **rolling deployment** replaces old `v1` replicas with `v2` replicas gradually in bounded batches rather than spinning up a 2x parallel Blue-Green fleet. In Kubernetes, two parameters govern the rollout pace: **`maxSurge`** (how many extra pods above desired count may run during update) and **`maxUnavailable`** (how many pods may be unavailable).

Setting **`maxUnavailable: 0`** and **`maxSurge: 25%`** (or `1` for small deployments) guarantees 100% serving capacity throughout the entire rollout.

learningJourney.title: Why Rolling Deploys Drop Requests Without Graceful Drain
learningJourney.explanation: In Kubernetes, removing a pod from `Endpoints` and sending `SIGTERM` happen **asynchronously in parallel**. If the app immediately closes its HTTP port on `SIGTERM` before `kube-proxy` or the cloud ALB updates iptables/targets (which takes 2–8 seconds), live clients hit `ECONNREFUSED` (`502`). Similarly, wrapping the app in a shell script without `exec` traps `SIGTERM` in `/bin/sh` (`PID 1`) so the app never drains and gets `SIGKILL`ed after 30s.

ideas.title: Always Use `exec` in Container Entrypoints
ideas.description: Ensure your application binary runs as `PID 1` (`CMD ["./server"]` or `exec python ...`) so it receives `SIGTERM` directly.

ideas.title: Readiness Probes Are Not Business-Logic Gates
ideas.description: A pod can pass `/readyz` while throwing 500s on `/checkout`—pair rolling updates with Argo Rollouts / Flagger SLO checks.

learningJourney.title: Where Rolling Deployments fit (and where Blue-Green/Canary win)
learningJourney.explanation: Use rolling updates for stateless microservices with backward-compatible APIs/schemas; use Blue-Green or Canary when mixed versions or unmonitored rollouts pose high risk.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Stateless Microservices & Worker Fleets
benefits: Zero-downtime updates using only 10–25% surge capacity instead of 2x fleet cost.
costs: Old `v1` and new `v2` pods serve traffic concurrently during the rollout window.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Stateful Singletons or Incompatible v1/v2 Protocols
benefits: Use Blue-Green or Recreate when two versions cannot coexist against shared state or schemas.
costs: Mixed-version serialization/DB mismatches cause silent corruption during rolling windows.

learningJourney.title: How `maxUnavailable: 0`, `preStop` & `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` are configured
learningJourney.explanation: Set `maxUnavailable: 0`, `maxSurge: 25%`, a `preStop` `sleep 10` hook, and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` strictly greater than `preStop + longest_request_timeout`.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 25%
  template:
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      containers:
        - name: api
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 10"]  # Wait for LB/kube-proxy removal
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /readyz, port: 8080 }
            periodSeconds: 5
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Rolling Update vs. Canary vs. Blue-Green
learningJourney.explanation: Balance extra compute cost against rollback speed and mixed-version exposure.

benefits: Built into Kubernetes with minimal extra compute (only `maxSurge`).
costs: Slow rollback (must roll forward/back pod-by-pod) and no built-in Prometheus SLO halt gate.

benefits: Holds at 5% traffic and auto-aborts on Prometheus 5xx/p99 regressions.
costs: Requires ingress traffic splitting and metric analysis templates.

benefits: Instant atomic rollback and zero mixed-version traffic.

learningJourney.title: Production example: PDB-Protected Rolling Update + Automated Halt
learningJourney.explanation: A production Deployment pairs `maxUnavailable: 0` with a `PodDisruptionBudget` (`minAvailable: 80%`), `preStop: sleep 10`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45`, and an Argo/Prometheus alert that halts `kubectl rollout` automatically if 5xx error rate rises.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** A **rolling deployment** replaces old `v1` replicas with `v2` replicas gradually in bounded batches rather than spinning up a 2x parallel Blue-Green fleet.

**How It Flows:** Think of Rolling Deployment Strategy as a clear step-by-step chain: K8s Controller -> Endpoints / LB -> Old Pod (v1) -> New Pod (v2) -> ACTIVE READY.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Set `maxUnavailable: 0` with `maxSurge > 0`, gate traffic with accurate `readinessProbe`s, and pair `preStop` sleep (5–15s) with `SIGTERM` graceful draining so zero in-flight requests hit 502 during pod termination.
